questions.q: Which Azure command creates a VNet along with its first subnet in a single call?
options: az network vnet create, using --subnet-name and --subnet-prefix
az network vnet subnet create, with no VNet required first
az group create, which creates both the resource group and the VNet
az vm create, which creates the VNet automatically if one is missing
questions.explain: az network vnet create takes --subnet-name and --subnet-prefix to create the VNet's first subnet in the same call, since Azure won't create a VNet with zero subnets.

questions.q: What is the AWS equivalent of az network vnet create for making the overall address block?
options: aws ec2 create-vpc, using --cidr-block
aws ec2 create-subnet, using --cidr-block
aws ec2 create-security-group
aws ec2 describe-subnets
questions.explain: aws ec2 create-vpc with --cidr-block sets up the VPC's overall address range, the AWS equivalent of az network vnet create's --address-prefix.

questions.q: Why does this lesson size the VNet/VPC at a /16 and only use a few /24 subnets out of it?
options: To leave room for subnets that will be added later, like monitoring, backup, or high-availability tiers
Because cloud providers require every VPC to be exactly a /16
Because /24 subnets are not supported inside a /16 VPC
To reduce the monthly cost of the VPC
questions.explain: Sizing with room to grow means allocating more address space than needed today, so future subnets don't force a disruptive redesign.

questions.q: What problem does under-sizing a VPC at 10.0.0.0/24 create later in the project?
options: There may not be enough address space left for a fourth or fifth subnet without redesigning the layout
The VPC will automatically expand itself to a /16 when needed
Nothing — subnet count has no relationship to the VPC's address block size
It only affects billing, not actual subnet creation
questions.explain: A /24 VPC has only 256 addresses total, which barely fits one subnet — adding more tiers later runs out of room fast.

questions.q: What do az network vnet subnet list and aws ec2 describe-subnets let you do?
options: Verify what subnets actually got deployed, with their CIDR ranges and availability zones, before building on top of them
Create new subnets directly
Delete a VNet or VPC and all its subnets at once
Automatically resize an existing subnet
questions.explain: Both commands list the existing subnets so you can confirm the deployment matches the plan before attaching NSGs or compute to it.
